knowledge:
- key_parameters: DE_ctrl_cond=Specifies which condition to use as the control in the DE comparison (e.g., 'heart') ;; filter_cutoff=CPM cutoff for filtering low-expressing genes (default is 1) ;; counts_filtered=Logical, set to TRUE if the user has already pre-filtered the count table to bypass ERSSA's filtering ;; comb_gen_repeat=Number of unique subsample combinations per replicate level (default is 30) ;; DE_software=Software to use for DE analysis, either 'edgeR' (default) or 'DESeq2' ;; num_workers=Number of CPUs/workers for parallel execution via BiocParallel ;; DE_cutoff_stat=Adjusted p-value (or FDR) cutoff for DEGs (default is 0.05) ;; DE_cutoff_Abs_logFC=Absolute log2 fold-change cutoff for DEGs (default is 1) ;; DE_save_table=Logical, set to TRUE to save DE analysis tables as CSV files ;; marginalPlot_stat=Statistic to plot in the marginal plot, either 'median' (default) or 'mean' ;; TPR_FPR_stat=Statistic to plot in the TPR/FPR plot, either 'mean' (default) or 'median'
- alternatives: edgeR=Default and faster DE software ;; DESeq2=Alternative DE software, preferred by setting DE_software='DESeq2' ;; genefilter=Can be used for pre-filtering counts before running ERSSA
- when_to_use: When you have an existing RNA-seq dataset with a certain number of replicates (N) and want to determine if you have sufficient biological replicates to capture most DEGs, or if adding more replicates would significantly increase discovery.
- pitfalls: High biological variance datasets may require increasing comb_gen_repeat (e.g., to 50) to reduce sensitivity to outliers, which increases runtime ;; Using the full dataset as the 'ground truth' for TPR/FPR calculations can be misleading if the dataset itself is underpowered (e.g., too few replicates to begin with, like N=5) ;; Running hundreds of DE comparisons can be very slow; users should use parallel processing (num_workers) to mitigate this ;; Small expected differences (e.g., weak stimulation) might yield very few DEGs at default logFC cutoffs, requiring the user to lower DE_cutoff_Abs_logFC (e.g., to 0.5)

workflows.name: erssa_sample_size_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform empirical RNA-seq sample size analysis by subsampling and running differential expression to determine replicate sufficiency.
input: count_table (R data.frame containing raw RNA-seq counts with genes as rows and sample IDs as columns)
condition_table (R data.frame containing sample IDs in column 1 and condition names in column 2)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the ERSSA package and prepare count and condition tables ;; 2. Set a random seed for reproducible subsampling ;; 3. Run the main erssa function to filter counts, generate subsamples, perform DE analysis, and identify DEGs ;; 4. Customize and save the resulting diagnostic plots (e.g., dot plot, marginal plot, intersect plot, TPR/FPR plot)
workflows.code:
library(ERSSA)

# GTEx dataset with 10 heart and 10 muscle samples
# "full"" dataset contains all ensembl genes
data(condition_table.full)
data(count_table.full)

# For test purposes and faster run time, we will use a smaller "partial" dataset
# 4 heart and 4 muscle samples
# partial dataset contains 1000 genes
data(condition_table.partial)
data(count_table.partial)

# NOTE: the figures are generated from the "full" dataset

head(count_table.full[,1:2])

condition_table.full

set.seed(1) # for reproducible subsample generation

ssa = erssa(count_table.partial, condition_table.partial, DE_ctrl_cond='heart')

# Running full dataset is skipped in the interest of run time
# ssa = erssa(count_table.full, condition_table.full, DE_ctrl_cond='heart')

library(ggplot2)

# Parse out plot 1
de_plot = ssa$gg.dotPlot.obj$gg_object 
# Change y-axis label to be more descriptive
de_plot = de_plot + ylab('Number of differentially expressed genes')

# Save the plot in the current working directory with new dimensions and a
# lower resolution.
ggsave(filename='ERSSA_plot_1_NumOfDEGenes.png',
     plot=de_plot, dpi=100, width = 15,
     height = 10, units = "cm")
